newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian opposition unites against government.
newsitem.headline: Albanian opposition unites against government.

text.p: Albania's opposition parties from across the political spectrum put aside their differences on Thursday and launched an unprecedented united front against the ruling Democrat government.

The Forum for Democracy alliance, made up of seven parties along with a group of anti-communist dissidents, demanded that Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his cabinet resign following the collapse of private pyramid investment schemes.
"What goes bankrupt should end and this government has gone economically, politically and judicially bankrupt," the head of the centre-right Democratic Alliance, Neritan Ceka, told a news conference.
"The government only wants to gain time. It has no solutions," he added, calling for a technocrat government to be set up to resolve the crisis followed by new elections.
The failure of the pyramid schemes has sent shockwaves through impoverished Albania with almost every family in this tiny Balkan state believed to have put money into the funds.
Opposition parties, including the main Socialist Party, teamed up on Thursday, the day after the government launched a wave of arrests in the wake of widespread rioting.
The democratic forum said President Sali Berisha had introduced a de facto state of emergency and urged the West not to come to the government's rescue.
"Tell your (Western) peoples not to pay any more for a dictatorship in the centre of Europe," Ceka said.
Most of the big opposition parties boycotted a general election last May, alleging widespread poll manipulation, intimidation and vote rigging by the Democrats.
Observers from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) also reported irregularities in the poll -- accusations dismissed by the ruling party.

Opposition parties have accused the government of committing economic suicide by allowing Albanians to sink millions of dollars into the risky pyramid schemes, which sprung up following the demise of the old communist regime in 1990.
"(The government) showed how not to build a market economy," Ceka told reporters.
"There is no economic perspective because we are facing an economic, political and moral crisis. If the government goes on, there will be a catastrophe," he added.
President Berisha said on Wednesday that the government was not involved in the schemes and said ministers alerted people at the end of last year when the risks became apparent.

He assured investors from two of the failed schemes, which have had their bank assets frozen, that they would get some of their money back. It appeared compensation would not be offered to investors from other funds which have also gone bankrupt but had no bank assets to seize.
